# Proton proton_10.0 - WOW64 with Vulkan & GStreamer for Termux (xuser)

- **Proton 分支**: proton_10.0
- **架构**: True WOW64 (同时支持 32 位和 64 位 Windows 应用程序)
- **平台**: Termux (Android)
- **图形 API**: Vulkan 支持已启用
- **多媒体**: 完整 GStreamer 支持
- **用户名**: xuser (已移除 Steam 优化)

✓ 真正的 WOW64 架构
✓ 同时支持 32 位和 64 位 Windows 应用程序
✓ Vulkan 图形 API 支持
✓ 完整的 GStreamer 支持
✓ 中文环境支持

解压后，将 `proton-proton-wine-10.0-4-b8fdff8e1f8-wow64-xuser` 文件夹放置在 Termux 的合适位置，并设置环境变量。

- 提交: c139ecff7e39b1a0e194826fccf83496e3dbbfa9
- 工作流: Wine and Proton 无bootBuilder

# X360 Mobile 0.6.5

This update focuses on more reliable profile and save imports, together with improvements to graphics processing and performance.

## Profiles and saved games

- Improved import reliability, including backups created with earlier versions of X360 Mobile.
- Clearer previews and confirmation before replacing existing profile or saved-game data.
- Stronger checks and recovery when an import is cancelled or interrupted, helping protect existing data.
- Preserves the original profile and saved-game ownership when restoring backups.

## Graphics and performance

- Improved graphics-work scheduling and reduced avoidable processing overhead.
- Added and refined graphics optimizations, evaluated using **GTA IV on Odin 2**.
- Further improvements to graphics-resource handling and pipeline reliability.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.4 — Hotfix 2
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.4 — Hotfix 2

This update brings general correctness, graphics, stability and efficiency improvements, developed and evaluated using **Split/Second** as a reference game. These are improvements to the emulator itself rather than fixes restricted to one title. Other games may also benefit, but broader compatibility and performance testing is still limited.

## Improvements

- Improved handling of demanding graphics workloads and reduced avoidable processing overhead.
- Corrected visual consistency and resource-handling issues, including an issue affecting frame interpolation.
- Improved the reliability of the touch-control layout editor.
- Added optional independent auto-hide for the Menu button.
- Reorganized Settings with fewer main categories and clearer access to game content, patches and advanced tools.

## Split/Second: still experimental

On the tested **Snapdragon 8 Gen 2** setup, Split/Second currently fluctuates around **8–18 FPS**, depending on the scene and the selected experimental settings. The game **still requires extensive further work to become playable on this SoC**. Occasional pauses and remaining graphical issues are still under investigation.

releases.body:
This release features many experimental/WIP Android improvements by @kleidis that you can test before they eventually get merged into [Azahar](https://github.com/azahar-emu/azahar). It also brings up various third-party dependencies to their latest major versions, and includes some very minor bug fixes.

There is also [a beta release](https://github.com/Borked3DS/Borked3DS/releases/tag/v2025.01.23-sdl-compat) that is the same as this one except that it incorporates the use of SDL3 via the SDL2 compatability layer. The intent is to port this project over to pure SDL3 eventually, but the compatability layer approach allows people to play around with things while waiting for the porting to be completed. This also gives this project a fallback in case SDL2 stops being supported upstream but new functionality such as gamepad support for new game controllers continues to be updated on the SDL3 branch.

### What's Changed
* Android: Some minor fixes by @rtiangha in https://github.com/Borked3DS/Borked3DS/pull/293
* renderer_opengl: Enable a couple of optimizations by @rtiangha in https://github.com/Borked3DS/Borked3DS/pull/294

releases.body:
Copperline 1.0.1 is the first maintenance release for 1.0. Most of it fixes problems reported against 1.0.0: an AGA display fetch error, a blitter race on fast CPUs, warm reboots on the A3000 and A4000, the 68060 FPU at reset, the copperhf hard-disk driver, and a window-resize hang on Windows. Menu settings are now remembered between launches, and screenshots save the picture as you see it.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.0.1.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version. Desktop `.clstate` files still load: the save-state format has not changed, and a 1.0.0 state resumes byte-for-byte as it does in 1.0.0.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.0
releases.body:
Copperline 1.0.0 is the first stable release. It follows two weeks of testing of 1.0.0-rc.1 and is the 23rd release since the source went public on 14 June.

This release adds Smart framing and native 1:1 screenshots, more control over where and how the window opens, VHD hard-disk images, a fix for AGA sprites that use scan-doubling, and a Check for updates button that only contacts GitHub when you press it.

## Copperline 1.0 at a glance

- **Machines:** A1000, A500, A500+, A600, A1200, A3000, A4000, CDTV and CD32, with OCS, ECS and AGA chipsets and 68000 to 68060 CPUs, FPUs and MMUs.
- **Accuracy:** the CPU and custom chips run on one colour-clock timeline, with the chip bus shared out cycle by cycle. Timing is checked against a real A1200, A4000 and CD32, and 45 test programs are compared pixel for pixel on every change.

DingooEmu v0.1.0

DingooEmu 首个正式版本，支持运行 Dingoo A320 平台的 `.app` 游戏文件，提供独立运行版和 libretro 核心两种使用方式。

## ✨ 新功能

### 核心模拟
- 实现兼容 Ingenic JZ4740 XBurst 的 MIPS32 CPU 解释器
- 支持解析和加载 Dingoo A320 `.app` 游戏容器
- 以 HLE 方式实现图形、输入、音频、计时、文件、任务和系统等 Dingoo SDK 功能
- 支持持久化游戏存档、事务式即时存档和金手指

### 图形与音频
- 支持 320×240 RGB565 帧缓冲，并输出 XRGB8888 画面
- 支持 PCM 音频播放、格式转换、音量控制和重采样
- 使用有界音频队列和背压机制改善连续播放的稳定性
- 支持无窗口截图和批量截图，可用于自动化测试与预览生成

### 独立运行版与 RetroArch

- libretro 核心支持视频、音频、RetroPad 输入、重置、持久化存档、即时存档和金手指
- 支持在 RetroArch 中实时调整音频、输入、日志和解释器诊断选项
- 提供 Windows、Linux、macOS、Android、iOS 和 webOS 构建

- 新增未知 SDK 调用汇总、严格执行策略和允许列表，便于定位未实现功能
- 新增可复现的 JSON/CSV 兼容性报告，以及确定性输入和 PCM 音频检查点

releases.body:
# Read the blog post at [FEX-Emu's Site!](https://fex-emu.com/FEX-2611/)
You know the drill, it's been around a month so that means we have a new release landing. A smattering of changes all over the codebase this time.
Let's see what's interesting!

## CPU core index through TPIDRRO_EL0
This is a fun feature that has come about primarily because Windows on ARM mandates this feature. The [TPIDRRO_EL0](https://support.arm.com/documentation/ddi0601/2026-09/AArch64-Registers/TPIDRRO-EL0--EL0-Read-Only-Software-Thread-ID-Register?lang=en) register
is an ARM system register that is readable by userspace that the kernel can set to whatever 64-bit value it wants. In particular under Windows it is
part of their [ABI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/arm64-windows-abi-conventions?view=msvc-170#system-registers) that this register must
contain the current CPU core index once read. This gives ARM64/ARM64ec applications a really quick way to read what core it is executing on. This is
kind of a funny thing that needs to exist because **technically** the MPIDR_EL1 register is supposed to accomplish the same task. Although this
register is kernel-mode only, through their [CPU feature register emulation](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/v5.8/arm64/cpu-feature-registers.html)
you can read this register on Linux with a bit of overhead. The problem with this register is that many vendors messed it up, and also it's not just
an index from zero to the number of cores in the system. So in the end the kernel actually only ever returns zero. On Linux, FEX will use the
**getcpu** syscall instead to get the CPU core index.

So what are we to do? ARM64 WINE applications need this register to be ABI compliant and FEX would like to use it for faster emulation of
RDPID/RDTSCP/CPUID. What does Linux do for this register? Turns out in the 15 years since ARM64 was introduced, the Linux kernel has hardcoded this
register to always be zero and be reserved for future work. S

# Read the blog post at [FEX-Emu's Site!](https://fex-emu.com/FEX-2610/)
We were a bit distracted this month with the [X.Org Developer's Conference](https://indico.freedesktop.org/event/12/) happening but we still managed
to get some work done. Let's jump in and see what has changed.

## JIT changes
This month brought some improvements to the JIT although less than typical. We added support for AVX-VNNI which is starting to get used by some game
libraries. We also optimized the SSE4.2 string operations so these are quite a bit faster. 3DNow! has been enabled again since we fixed the last known
bug with it. We also improved emulation on the x87 FXAM instruction since apparently Mono uses it to detect denormals for some reason. Additionally a
peephole optimization to improve a common case of an unmasked AVX gather instruction which some sound libraries rely on.

We also now have a software fallback for RDRAND and RDSEED instructions. This isn't enabled by default as the performance isn't as good as a hardware
implementation but it's useful for programs that mandate these instructions to exist. Also useful for platforms with Qualcomm Oryon where their RNG
implementation is bugged and doesn't return real values.

Plus a couple of other minor changes for future work. In total a fairly light month for JIT improvements.

## Disk cache improvements
This month also had a large smattering of disk cache improvements. Now when the disk cache is enabled it will automatically limit its cache size to
1GB, where we will then stop caching at that point. This is configurable in the INI options for more or less space to be consumed, but because some
edge cases allow it to have unbounded growth, it seems like a good balance at 1GB. We also added an optional memory buffer for caching; this allows an
in-memory cache for hot blocks. This is only worth using if a game stutters frequently from JIT invocations and you have spare RAM to allow some
additional caching.

# Read the blog post at [FEX-Emu's Site!](https://fex-emu.com/FEX-2608/)
After what felt like a very quick month, it's time for another FEX release. We're busy writing improvements for next month's release already, so let's
not distract for too long and smash through these changes!

## Removal of deprecated FEXInterpreter binary
Back in the [FEX-2510](/FEX-2510) release we completely removed a **FEXLoader** binary with a deprecation of the **FEXInterpreter** binary, renaming it to
just **FEX**. We kept the FEXInterpreter binary around for a while because downstream projects had hardcoded the binary in their scripts and we wanted to give
some time for them to migrate. After nearly a year we're hoping that everyone has migrated to the new binary name. If your project is still using the
old binary name then we recommend fix them!

## The typical JIT improvements
As typical there are a bunch of JIT changes this month. Let's breakdown  what was fixed.

- Use SVE XAR for SHA1 emulation as a minor optimization.
- Fix JIT telemetry value unconstrained predictable problem on ARMv8.0
  - Would only cause some missed telemetry on ARMv8.0 platforms, very minor.
- Optimize VMOVMASKPD/PS instructions.
  - Cutting from 11/10 instructions down to 7.
- Fix incorrect emulation of BFP store instruction
- Fixes crash if `ProcessorID` IR op was encountered on WINE
  - Silly little assert check that crashed.
- A bunch more improvements to hardware with 256-bit SVE
- Actually a ton of little bug fixes and edge cases getting patched up.

## Fix VirtualProtect on win32
This change is fairly spicy because it means some of our memory protections were silently failing under WINE. With this fixed, it should fix some
weird edge case crashes that weren't able to be explained.

## Fix overwriting memory region in allocation tracking
This is a bit of a weird case where FEX's memory allocations on 48-bit VA systems were  *silently* only ever using one allocation region.

# Read the blog post at [FEX-Emu's Site!](https://fex-emu.com/FEX-2607/)
Time certainly goes by quicker than you'd expect. We even managed to skip last months release because we were busy doing other things. Let's take that
as an example and fly through the changes that we did over these past two months!

## Optimizations and fixes for 256-bit SVE2 hardware
While this hardware doesn't exist yet, we know it is an inevitability that it will at some point. While we switched gears a couple years ago to
implement AVX using 128-bit operations, we never removed this code. In-fact we've been spending a bunch of effort on it fixing bugs and optimizing it
so that once hardware ships it won't be broken. We have now validated extensively that all AVX instructions now zero extend their results as expected
and optimized a bunch of the instructions so they generate faster code. We think it's now at a point that in the common case the code will be faster
than our 128-bit emulation, but there is definitely still some more work todo. SVE2.1 provides a significant improvement to how shuffles operate and
we haven't gotten those implemented yet. Because there aren't any 256-bit SVE2 hardware on the market, we might even require SVE2.1 or SVE2.2 for this
class of hardware. We'll of course still maintain our 128-bit path for lower-end hardware of course.

## Highlights

- **Disk images are kept unmodified with a save directory.** With `-saveDir`, what the software writes goes to an overlay file there and the image is only read. Overlays store only the tracks or blocks written and are tied to a checksum of their image. This also makes writable the disks that could not be written before: inside a zip or gzip, loaded from a URL, or embedded in the executable.
- **DOS 3.3 boots in five seconds.** The Disk II motor keeps turning for about a second after the drive is turned off, like the 556 timer of the real controller, and the data latch no longer reads the same nibble twice. It is built from source and is not in the release archives. See [the libretro page](https://github.com/ivanizag/izapple2/blob/master/doc/frontend_libretro.md) and [the Mac guide](https://github.com/ivanizag/izapple2/blob/master/doc/frontend_libretro_macos.md).

What's new in 0.78

For players
- **32-bit devices:** one APK now holds both ARMv8 (arm64-v8a) and ARMv7
  (armeabi-v7a). Android picks the right one on install, so 64-bit devices
  always run the 64-bit version. OpenGL ES 3.0 is still required.
- **Screen orientation:** the setting now applies to the launcher as well as
  the game and takes effect at once. Auto respects the system rotation lock.
- **Sound:** the audio buffer margin now adapts to the device.
- **Launcher:** new Advanced screen with a Debug mode switch. With it off,
  nothing is written to the log.
- **Logs:** new screen under Data to export, share or send logs to the
  developer, or clear them.

Under the hood
- **Most of the game is now ported C++:** - game code is moving from recompiled to ported native ARM code.
- **Old processor code removed:** x87 emulation is gone from the generated
  code, and the whole game runs in 24-bit floating point. MMX, CPU detection
  and the Pentium FDIV workarounds are removed too.

Known limits
- ARMv7 has only been tested in the 32-bit mode of a 64-bit phone, not on a
  real 32-bit device, so speed on older hardware is unknown.
- Network play is not compatible anymore with PC Mod
